stem: Marks scored by 40 students in a class test are given in the following frequency distribution: 0-10: 4 students; 10-20: 10 students; 20-30: 16 students; 30-40: 6 students; 40-50: 4 students. What is the quartile deviation of the marks?

per_option_rationale.rationale: 14 is the inter-quartile range (Q3 - Q1 = 30 - 16 = 14). The student correctly found Q1 and Q3 but forgot to divide by 2 when computing the quartile deviation.
16 is Q1 itself. The student correctly located Q1 = 16 using the quartile formula but mistakenly reported Q1 as the quartile deviation.

8 arises from using the (n+1)/4 formula for grouped data (which applies to raw data): position 41/4 = 10.25, Q1 = 16.25; position 30.75, Q3 = 30.47; QD = (30.47-16.25)/2 approximately 7.1, which students sometimes round or re-compute as 8 due to a further slip.

explanation: For grouped data, n = 40. Q1 position = n/4 = 10. The cumulative frequency just below 10 is 4 (class 0-10). Q1 falls in class 10-20: Q1 = 10 + ((10-4)/10)*10 = 16. Q3 position = 3n/4 = 30. The cumulative frequency just below 30 is 14 (class 0-20). Q3 falls in class 20-30: Q3 = 20 + ((30-14)/16)*10 = 30. QD = (30-16)/2 = 7.

explanation_sections.punchline: For grouped data, quartile positions use n/4 and 3n/4 (not (n+1)/4), and quartile values are found by linear interpolation within the class.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: grouped data QD. Step 1: compute Q1 position = n/4 = 10, find the class containing the 10th value (10-20, CF before = 4, f = 10). Interpolate: Q1 = L + ((n/4 - CF_prev)/f)*h = 10 + (6/10)*10 = 16. Step 2: compute Q3 position = 3n/4 = 30, class 20-30 (CF before = 14, f = 16). Interpolate: Q3 = 20 + (16/16)*10 = 30. Step 3: QD = (30-16)/2 = 7.
explanation_sections.lesson: For grouped frequency data, always use n/4 for quartile positions (not (n+1)/4), then interpolate inside the identified class.
explanation_sections.timing: 75-90 seconds. Key trap: reporting IQR = 14 instead of QD = 7. Note: (30-14)/16 = 1 exactly, making Q3 = 30 a particularly clean result here.
